title: The same document model runs unchanged in a browser host and a headless server host because the host owns the runtime
content:
A document model is a schema plus reducers. Nothing in it names a database, a transport, a DOM, or a credential. That absence is deliberate, and it is what lets one package run in a browser and on a headless server with no per-host variant.

## Where the difference lives instead

Everything environment-specific is the host's, not the model's:

- **Connect** renders the model's editor components and signs actions with the user's identity. It supplies the DOM, the modals, the drive browser.
- **Switchboard** exposes the same documents over GraphQL and MCP so agents, back-ends, and integrations reach them without a browser, and it runs processors server-side.

Both embed a Reactor. Both feed the same reducers. The model, as the Academy puts it, "doesn't know which host it's in, and it doesn't need to."

## Why it matters

This is the practical payoff of keeping the Reactor a plain library rather than a service. Because the host owns the runtime, you get to choose the runtime — and you can have more than one at the same time. A finance ledger written once is simultaneously an offline-capable browser app and an API-addressable server resource, without a second implementation to keep in sync.

## The mental model

Think of the model as a cartridge and hosts as consoles. The cartridge carries logic and shape; the console supplies power, display, and controllers. Asking "which host is this model for?" is the wrong question — it is a category error, like asking which screen a function is for.

## The design pressure it creates

Portability only holds if you honour the boundary. A reducer that reaches for `window`, a wall clock, or a network call quietly binds the model to one runtime and breaks the property. That is the deeper reason reducers must be pure: purity is not fastidiousness, it is what keeps the cartridge playable on every console.

_Source: apps/academy/docs/academy/02-Learn/02-architecture/02-host-applications.mdx (Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45)._
description: Connect renders the editor and signs with the user's identity; Switchboard exposes the same document over an API and runs processors. The model never learns which host it is in.
